events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWRLX

The National Weather Service in Charleston has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southern Morgan County in southeastern Ohio...
Northern Washington County in southeastern Ohio...

* Until 700 AM EDT.

* At 256 AM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
0.5 and 1.5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts
up to 0.5 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Marietta, Beverly, Matamoras, Lowell, Stockport, Macksburg, Lower
Salem, Devola and New Matamoras.

This includes Interstate 77 in Ohio between mile markers 4 and 17.

events.region: Southern Sangre de Cristo Mountains; East Slopes Sangre de Cristo Mountains
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...The Southern and East Slopes of the Sangre de Cristo
Mountains, including the Hermits Peak Calf Canyon burn scar.

* WHEN...From 11 AM MDT this morning through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks on and below the
Hermits Peak Calf Canyon burn scar.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Storms with heavy rainfall rates in excess of 1 inch per hour are
expected to develop over the peaks of the Sangre de Cristo
Mountains then slowly drift eastward over the Hermits Peak Calf
Canyon burn scar during the early to mid-afternoon.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Knox; Stark; Peoria; Marshall; Woodford; Fulton; Tazewell; McLean; De Witt; Piatt; Champaign; Vermilion
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, and west central
Illinois, including the following counties, in central Illinois,
De Witt, Marshall, McLean, Peoria, Piatt, Stark, Tazewell and
Woodford. In east central Illinois, Champaign and Vermilion. In
west central Illinois, Fulton and Knox.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM CDT this morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy rain has fallen across portions of central Illinois
over the past few days, including a streak of 3 to 7 inches,
locally higher, that fell over the past 24 hours from Canton
to Bloomington to Danville. Showers and thunderstorms will
produce an additional 1 to 3 inches of rain into the morning
across portions of central Illinois. Saturated grounds will
lead to rapid runoff from any additional rainfall. Flash
flooding and rapid rises on area rivers and streams are
possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Extreme Western Allegany; Central and Eastern Allegany; Hampshire; Hardy; Western Grant; Eastern Grant; Western Mineral; Eastern Mineral
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of western Maryland, including the following
areas, Central and Eastern Allegany and Extreme Western Allegany
and eastern West Virginia, including the following areas, Eastern
Grant, Eastern Mineral, Hampshire, Hardy, Western Grant and
Western Mineral.

* WHEN...From 6 AM this morning to noon EDT today. Additional
thunderstorms with heavy rain are possible late this afternoon and
evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A cluster of thunderstorms producing very heavy rain is
approaching the area from southeast Ohio and northern West
Virginia. These thunderstorms have been producing rainfall
amounts of 2 to 3 inches per hour. These storms may affect
parts of the area this morning, resulting in similar rainfall
amounts and a risk for flash flooding.
- Please visit www.weather.gov/safety/flood for flood safety
and preparedness information.
